solver.kind: blind AI solver A (separate agent, answer-free packet)

S002-01.notes: Weighing several explanations and acknowledging record limits = measured. Strident/dogmatic are opposites; cursory contradicts careful weighing. Single-word choices, no length tell.

flags: minor: C is noticeably the longest and most detailed choice; can be spotted by length/form alone.
S002-02.notes: Assumption (trehalose) -> evidence against (little/none found) -> alternative (glass-forming proteins). A wrong (alternative supported), B no limitations listed, D no comparison.

flags: minor: D is the longest and only hedged choice; somewhat spottable by form.
S002-03.notes: Text 2 grants early improvement but says gains vanish within a few years; one-year data is accurate but too short. A contradicts Text 2 (times improve at first); B, C unsupported.

flags: minor: D is the only choice containing both halves of the claim (rot + bloom) and is the longest; very easy.
S002-04.notes: D shows decay (sag with rot) and productivity (still they bloom). A decay only; B productivity only; C irrelevant.

flags: minor: B is far longer than other choices and is the only one mentioning both percentage and absolute change; spottable by length.
S002-05.notes: Verified: A +3,000 (25%), B +4,500 (15%), C +2,400 (30%). C largest percentage, B largest absolute. Numbers in B are accurate.

S002-06.notes: Complete independent clause followed by a list -> colon. Semicolon needs an independent clause after; 'which' and 'and' create ungrammatical constructions.

S002-07.notes: Subject 'Each' is singular; intervening plural 'volunteers' is a distractor. Past tense fits 'at the end of the festival'. 'was'.

S002-08.notes: 'the two' requires plural; possessive of plural -> scientists'. 'scientists's' nonstandard; 'scientist's' singular; 'scientists' lacks possessive.

flags: minor: 'On the contrary' is defensible (attendance contradicts the critics' prediction), but a more common SAT key would be 'However,' or 'In fact,'. Consider whether 'On the contrary' sounds natural enough to test-takers; it typically rebuts a stated proposition, which it does here, so it is acceptable.
S002-09.notes: Second sentence contradicts the critics' prediction; only contrast option is C. Similarly/Therefore/For example are wrong relationships.

flags: minor: A is the only choice that both introduces the painter and names the work, and is dramatically longer than the rest; trivially spottable by length.
S002-10.notes: Goal requires introducing Adeyemi (to unfamiliar audience) and her best-known work. B names work but doesn't introduce her; C, D omit her.

S002-11.notes: Text 2 doesn't dispute quick quiz gains but says memorized definitions are forgotten within weeks -> question lasting gains. C too absolute; D concerns speed, which Text 2 doesn't address (it addresses retention); A unsupported.

flags: minor: D is the longest choice; mild length tell.
S002-12.notes: Vacancy chain: each crab takes the next-larger shell, so one new shell upgrades several crabs. B contradicts the chain; C contradicts lining up by size; A unsupported.
